chunks.text: Today, I will teach you how to order coffee, ask questions, and have a smooth conversation in English at a coffee shop.
This episode is for A1 -level English learners, so I will speak slowly and clearly.
How to order food and ask about ingredients, how to pay and understand prices, how to ask for Wi -Fi and a table, how to politely make small talk.
Entering the coffee shop and greeting the staff.
When you walk into a coffee shop, you might hear a friendly greeting.
What can I get for you today?
Can I see the menu please?
Can I order here, or do I need to sit down first?
Some coffee shops have menus on the wall, while others have printed menus at the counter.
Now, let's practice how to order a drink.
I'd like a black coffee with no sugar.
Can I have a tea with lemon?
Would you like sugar or milk?
No sugar, but I'd like oat milk please.
Many coffee shops offer different types of milk, such as almond milk, oat milk, and soy milk.
Many coffee shops sell pastries, sandwiches, and desserts.
I'd like a chocolate muffin please.
What kind of sandwiches do you have?
Can I get a cookie and a coffee?
Do you have any vegan snacks?
We have vegan brownies and oat cookies.
If you have food allergies, always ask before ordering.
After ordering, you need to pay.
Can I pay with a card?
Can I have the receipt please?
Some coffee shops don't accept cash, so it's good to have a card or mobile payment app.
Asking for Wi -Fi and a table.
If you want to sit and work, you may need to ask about Wi -Fi or a place to sit.
The password is on the receipt.
Some coffee shops limit Wi -Fi time to one or two hours, so check before sitting down.
Picking up your order and saying thank you.
When your order is ready, the barista will call your name.
Can I get a napkin please?
If they get your order wrong, say, excuse me?
I ordered a latte, not a black coffee.
Making small talk in a coffee shop.
You might want to chat with the barista or other customers.
Is this place always this busy?
This cafe has a great atmosphere.
Yes, I come here every morning before work.
In English -speaking countries, small talk is common in coffee shops.
Final tips for visiting a coffee shop.
Always say please and thank you.
Check the menu before ordering to decide quickly.
If the shop is busy, wait in line patiently.
Small talk can be a great way to practice English.
That's the end of today's episode.
Now you know how to order coffee and snacks in English.
Next time you visit a coffee shop, try using these phrases.
If you enjoyed this episode, subscribe and share it with your friends.
